name: Coefficient-Ratio and Source-Spectral Identity
statement: For a nonempty union-closed class and fixed rooted ratios $q$, the threshold of a coefficient array is $T_C(a)=\max\{1/\alpha_C(q),\beta_C(q)\}$. Consequently $\tau(C)^2=d_{\mathrm{sp}}(C)$. All union-closed reflections have the same optimized source-spectral value, and whenever one exists $\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(C)=\tau(C)^2$.
proof: At ratio threshold $t$, the separated positive and negative source systems are feasible exactly when $\alpha>1/t$ and $\beta<t$. Uniformly scaling $q$ reduces the optimization to $\inf_{\lambda>0}\max\{1/(\lambda\alpha),\lambda\beta\}=\sqrt{\beta/\alpha}$, including zero and infinite endpoint conventions.
